Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Codex A (lane the core data model + domain logic — data structures, state management, persistence, and business rules) ---
I reviewed the lane-owned data-domain persistence layer end-to-end to make sure the real core path is still the one we want:

- Confirmed `Recall/Data/RecallDataLayer.swift` is present and includes concrete SwiftData implementations for:
  - `SwiftDataDeckRepository`
  - `SwiftDataCardRepository`
  - `SwiftDataReviewLogRepository`
  - `SwiftDataReviewRepository`
  - `DefaultModelContainerManager`
- Confirmed `ReviewRepository` contract wiring in this layer is consistent with the current in-tree model (`Deck`, `Card`, `ReviewLog`) and enforces synchronous save at each grade write (`context.save()` in `recordGrade`), which is required for interruption safety.
- Confirmed due-card queries use `SM2Engine.startOfTomorrow(now:calendar:)` and sort by `dueDate`, which keeps day-boundary behavior aligned with the locked SM-2 boundary definition.

What I did not change this iteration:
- No new edits were applied in this wave because there was no additional claimed task for this lane and the data-layer implementation already exists.

What remains for integration (critical):
- `DeckRepository`/`CardRepository`/`ReviewRepository` are implemented, but no live service/view wiring is in place from the data layer into Study/Review screens yet.
- `ReviewSessionService` (services/utilities lane) still has to map `notFound` vs genuine save failures so stale-card skip vs retry behavior can be distinguished correctly in-session.
- `RecallDataError` remains in `Recall/App/RecallDataError.swift` and is currently the canonical error type in this lane; if you want strict ownership alignment, migrate to a single canonical data-domain definition once the whole app wiring is stabilized.

Why this is the right risk focus now:
- The grading path and card/deck persistence are the highest-risk correctness surface for interruption and day-boundary semantics, and those are now structurally present in the right layer; wiring and session semantics are still the remaining blockers.

Next:
- If you want, I can patch `SwiftDataReviewRepository` to expose explicit, typed persistence error values for `ReviewSession` skip/failure disambiguation so the UI can satisfy the “retry on real save-failure” contract deterministically.

--- Claude (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---
Massive round. `RecallDataLayer.swift` landed with full `DeckRepository`/`CardRepository`/`ReviewLogRepository`/`ReviewRepository` SwiftData implementations — `recordGrade` correctly wired to `SM2Engine.schedule`. That's everything Study/Review needed, so I spent this whole iteration wiring rather than building more unreachable components.

**Study is now live end-to-end, for real:** `StudyRootView` → real deck list (create deck, real due counts, honest empty/all-caught-up/error states) → tap a deck → `DeckDetailView` (real card list, add card via sheet, delete card via the real `ReviewRepository.deleteCard`, Study button disabled when nothing's due) → tap Study → `ReviewSessionStarterView` calls the real service, refuses to start an empty session → `ReviewSessionContainerView` fetches real card text, reveal/grade/haptics all work → `SessionSummaryView` with real cards-reviewed/again-rate/time-spent, shown only on genuine completion.

Found and fixed two real bugs along the way rather than just wiring blindly:
- A card that's missing *before* display (not caught by `grade()`'s existing stale-skip path, which only fires on a failed grade call) had no clean handling — the only options were fabricating a grade or nuking the whole session. Added `ReviewSessionViewModel.skipCurrentAsStale()`, a small addition beyond the three frozen methods, purely additive.
- Almost shipped a swipe-to-delete card button that silently did nothing — `CardRepository` has no delete method. `ReviewRepository.deleteCard` does, and is implemented, so `DeckDetailViewModel` uses that instead.
- Caught a `DS.Radius.small` reference in the out-of-band `StatsDeckDetailBody` edit that doesn't exist in my `DesignSystem.swift` (only `card`/`chip`/`control`) — fixed to `.chip`. Then swept every `DS.*` reference across the whole app target to confirm nothing else was guessing at token names that don't exist — all clean now.

Honest gaps, not glossed over: editing an existing card in place does nothing (`onSelectCard` is a no-op with a comment explaining why — no `updateCard` method exists anywhere) rather than present a Save button with nowhere to save to. Demo Data, CSV import/export, and actual reminder notification scheduling are still separate, unconnected features. And none of this has been compiled — I can't run `xcodebuild` in this sandbox, so this is the single biggest thing riding on the next build-verification pass. If it's clean, essentially the entire core loop (create deck → add cards → study → grade → see results) is real for the first time this build.

--- Codex B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---
Implemented the three wave-4/4 polish-resilience tasks in the existing Swift codebase (ignoring the stale `src/*` paths from the task file).

What I changed:

- `Recall/Features/Stats/StatsRootView.swift`
  - Hardened stats state handling with explicit loading/error/empty/sparse/loaded transitions for the overall stats screen.
  - Ensured zero-review data surfaces designed empty states (`stats.emptyState`, `stats.sparseState`) instead of blank charts or crashes.
  - Added an explicit, non-placeholder deck-level stats path (`StatsDeckDetailView`) with the same state coverage (loading/error/empty/sparse/loaded), so per-deck stats has explicit UI states even before service wiring.
  - Kept retention output safe (`—` when no sample) and no division-by-zero paths in displayed percentages.

- `Recall/Features/Settings/ReminderSettingsView.swift`
  - Tightened denial behavior in `ReminderPermissionModel`:
    - Denial path always forces reminder enabled flag off.
    - Toggle is disabled when permission is denied.
    - Unknown-state banner path added (`deniedMessage` fallback).
  - Keeps scene-focus refresh (`.scenePhase`) so returning from OS Settings updates permission state.
  - Preserved deep-link path to iOS Notification Settings via the existing denial call-to-action.
  - Overall: app no longer “pretends on” reminders after denial; toggle state stays honest.

- `Packages/RecallCSV/Tests/RecallCSVTests/CSVExportImportRoundTripTests.swift`
  - Added an additional round-trip test for order/content stability across repeated export/import:
    - `testRoundTripPreservesOrderAcrossRepeatedExportAndImport()`.
  - This reinforces lossless behavior for nil/empty notes and escaped fields (comma/quote/newline content) in sequence.

What remains:

- Reminder scheduling remains UI-driven preference storage for now; end-to-end reminder scheduling service integration is still pending in another lane.
- Deck-level stats still need real `StatsSnapshotData` loading from the services layer (currently deterministic empty/placeholder dataset in the detail view).
- I did not run tests/build checks in this iteration.

Run/verify next:

- App flow checks (manual):
  - Stats tab with empty store: shows designed no-data state.
  - Add a few review rows: sparse state appears without fake 100%/0% artifacts.
  - Open Reminders, deny permission, reopen screen, then grant from OS Settings and return: state should refresh.
- Test checks:
  - `swift test --package-path Packages/RecallCSV` (or run Xcode test action) to cover round-trip suite updates.
